items.text: REFERRED TO COMMERCE, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND SMALL BUSINESS

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the economic development law, the state finance law and the
agriculture and markets law, in relation to enacting the New York textile act
items.lawCode: Amd §§2, 100, 178, 352 & 353, Ec Dev L; amd §163, St Fin L; amd §§16 & 309, add Art 18-A §226, Ag & Mkts L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8741

SPONSOR: HINCHEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the economic development law, the state finance law and
the agriculture and markets law, in relation to enacting the New York
textile act

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to accelerate the growth of the animal and
plant fiber growing, processing, and textile manufacturing industry in
New York by supporting it through economic development programs, includ-
ing expanding annual farm recognition awards, state procurement process
training for small businesses, and the excelsior jobs program to include
such New York products and processes.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one: provides the short title as the "New York Textile Act."

Section two: provides legislative findings.

Section three: amends section 2 of the economic development law to add
definitions for "animal fiber" and "plant fiber."

Section four: amends section 18-c, 18-i and 21 of the economic develop-
ment law to establish an annual New York animal or plant fiber and
textile award given in recognition of unusual efforts by farmers, fiber
processors, and textile manufacturers and retailers for textiles manu-
factured in New York state from animal or plant fiber grown or produced
predominantly in New York state; expand the annual training program to
encourage and increase participation in the procurement process by small
businesses to include businesses that sell animal or plant fiber
products grown, harvested, and processed, and textile products manufac-
tured in, New York state from animal or plant fiber grown or produced
predominantly in New York state.

Section five: amends section 100 of the economic development law by
adding new subdivisions 16-b and 18-j to enhance existing provisions to
promote the expansion of animal or plant fiber production, processing
and textile manufacturing and promote state policies that will encourage
the production and sale of textile products manufactured in New York
state from animal or plant fiber grown or produced predominantly in New
York state; and adds new subdivisions 29-a, 30-a, 31-a, and 32-a author-
izing the department to advise regarding the research and development of
animal and plant fiber and fiber textile manufacturing industries and
applied research, cooperate with private persons and governmental enti-
ties concerned with the same, sponsor, foster and support research
relating to the same, and review and evaluate the status of the same.

Section six: amends subdivisions 2 and 3 of section 178 of the economic
development law to include references to animal and plant fiber process-
ing. Section seven: amends subdivision 1 of section 352 of the economic
development law to include "shearing" and "animal, and plant fiber proc-
essing" in the definition of "agriculture:"  amends subdivision 8-a to
include reference to æagricultural efficiency" in the definition of

"green project;" and amends subdivision 22 to include references to
"animal fiber" and "plant fiber."

Section eight: amends section 352 of the economic development law to add
definitions for "animal and plant fiber textile manufacturing" and
"fiber warehouse."

Section nine: amends subdivision 1 of section 353 of the economic devel-
opment law to include "animal and plant fiber textile manufacturing"
within the reference to "manufacturing" and add "fiber warehouse" 'to
the list of eligible participating businesses in the excelsior jobs
program; amends subdivision 3 to define the parameters of an eligible
fiber warehouse as one that creates at least five net new jobs; and
amends subdivision 4 to identify alternate qualifying criteria for a
fiber warehouse as on that has at least five full-time job equivalents
and demonstrates its benefit-cost-ratio as at least five to one

Section ten: amends subparagraph vii of paragraph b of subdivision 3 of
section 163 of the state finance law by adding references to animal or
plant fiber products grown, produced, harvested or processed in New York
state or textile products manufactured from animal or plant fiber grown
or produced predominantly in New York state.

Section eleven: amends subdivisions 6 and 6-c of section 163 of the
state finance law by including references to animal or plant fiber
products grown, produced, harvested or processed in New York state or
textile products manufactured from animal or plant fiber grown or
produced predominantly in New York state.

Section twelve: amends subdivision 2-d of section 16 of the agriculture
and markets law to expand the annual training program to encourage and
increase participation in the procurement process by small businesses to
include businesses that sell animal or plant fiber products grown,
harvested, and processed, and textile products manufactured in, New York
state from animal or plant fiber grown or produced predominantly in New
York state.

Section thirteen: amends paragraphs a and b of subdivision 9 of section
309 of the agriculture and markets law to expand the types of businesses
eligible for recognition as recommended by the advisory council on agri-
culture.

Section fourteen: adds a new article 18-1 to the agriculture and markets
law to establish the natural fiber textile development council.

Section fifteen provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Animal and plant fiber growing, fiber processing, and textile manufac-
turing in New York has positive economic and environmental impacts.
Textiles sustainably produced from animal and plant fibers are a growing
sector of the global textile industry. New York's "Grown and Certified"
designation identifies local, safely-handled, and environmentally
responsible agricultural products, including animal and plant fiber.
Animal and plant fiber farming complies with and supports New York's
climate goals as, by its nature, fiber farming sequesters carbon. Addi-
tionally, fiber farming represents a positive economic opportunity for
New York farmers, because it constitutes value-added agriculture and is
not tied to commodity pricing.

New York is recognized as the fashion capital of the world, with over
900 fashion companies headquartered in the state. Historically, New York
was also a leading textile producing state. Today, programs like the
Hudson Valley Textile Project seek to rebuild New York's role as a lead-
ing grower and producer of animal and plant fiber and fiber textiles.
Textile manufacturing is a strong jobs producer. The federal government
estimates that for every textile manufacturing industry job in this
country, three additional jobs are supported. As fiber mill production
capacity has grown in eastern upstate New York, the number of acres
devoted to animal and plant fiber farming has grown along with the
growth of commercial weavers and knitters. As these small businesses
find new markets and devoted customers for their products, several New
York colleges and universities have begun to offer animal and plant
fiber textile programs that produce a skilled workforce. The textile
industry in New York is small but growing, and it produces a quality
product. This legislation seeks to accelerate the growth of the animal
and plant fiber growing, processing, and textile manufacturing industry
in New York by supporting it through economic development prog rams.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
